download_method: Public Kaggle API HTTPS GET without authentication; AMZN dataset ZIP and Retailrocket individual events.csv ZIP. ZIP contents extracted byte-for-byte.

datasets.title: Amazon Stock Price
datasets.selected_use: Stock-market time series: predict next trading-day adjusted close from a rolling historical window.
caveats: Despite the publisher subtitle Real Time Price, the downloaded snapshot ends on 2023-12-05.
Trading dates are irregular in calendar time: weekends and holidays must not be invented as observed stock prices.
The publisher lists USD prices but provides no detailed upstream market-data provenance.
This is an academic forecasting exercise; compare the RNN with a last-observation baseline and make no claim of profitable investment performance.

datasets.title: Retailrocket recommender system dataset
datasets.timestamp_encoding: Unix epoch milliseconds; converted to UTC for reproducibility, not inferred store local time.
datasets.granularity: One timestamped visitor-item event per row
datasets.selected_use: Customer behavior over time: aggregate observed view/addtocart/transaction events hourly, then forecast next-hour transaction-event count from historical hourly behavior.
caveats: Raw rows are not chronologically sorted; sort or resample on timestamp before making sequences.
Missing transactionid on nonpurchase events is expected and must not cause those rows to be dropped.
Transaction event counts refer to purchase events/line items, not necessarily unique orders or unique purchasers.
Hourly aggregation describes population-level behavior; it does not predict an individual customer journey.
The dataset covers only about 4.5 months and may contain abnormal traffic.
The first and last observed clock periods are partial and should be excluded or clearly flagged.
Only events.csv was downloaded. Item properties and category tree are unnecessary for the selected aggregate forecast.
The source identifies this as real ecommerce data with anonymized/hashed values; retain source attribution and the listed noncommercial/share-alike license.

modeling_recommendations: Split chronologically by target timestamp, for example 70 percent train / 15 percent validation / 15 percent test; never randomly split time windows.
Fit feature and target transformations on training observations only. Use validation for model choice and keep test targets untouched until final evaluation.
Inputs for each target must end before the target time. Validation/test windows may use earlier known observations, but no future values.
Hourly customer behavior forecast: include previous day and previous week seasonal baselines when enough history exists.
Report MAE/RMSE in original units, plots of actual versus predicted targets, train/validation loss, and temporal train/validation/test boundaries.
selection_rationale: The brief requires one customer-behavior-over-time dataset and one stock dataset. Retailrocket directly records customer actions over time, and Amazon provides the stock dataset.
